open_points.subject: personal-data disclosure for direct agent access to microservices
open_points.text: “Personal data — values of class `personal_data` (K-14) reach an agent only as digest and class; the owner alone reads them.” contradicts “the kernel neither gives nor checks it, and its personal-data promise (K-14) covers what the kernel itself returns.”
open_points.question: Does the prohibition on agents receiving personal-data values apply to their direct, service-granted access outside the kernel, or only to values returned through the kernel surface?
options: The prohibition applies only to the kernel surface; direct service access follows the service’s and owner’s authorization.
The prohibition applies globally, so services and the owner must never grant an agent direct access to personal-data values.
open_points.default_guess: Treat K-14 as a kernel-surface guarantee only, because the changed exclusion explicitly places direct service access outside the kernel’s authority.
